analysis:
Examined the provider-side stop-string scoping change. EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift (head lines 14-32) now passes `stopStringScope` into the static matcher. When a scope is set, it replays `StopHoldback.ingest` and returns the candidate found at the stop boundary. This scope-aware path is only for reporting which stop sequence ended generation. The unscoped path (head 33-58) is unchanged. EngineV2Bridge+Submission.swift (head 249-250) adds `stopStringScope` to the CBv2 request. This is a client-visible stop-matching semantic for GPT-OSS: stops match only in the Harmony `final` channel, per the docs. It is not a trust-boundary change.

Security relevance is low. Stop strings are client-supplied and the scope only restricts where they match. Possible effects are availability (a stop not matching could run to the token limit, bounded by max_tokens and the existing leases, T-010) and output-integrity correctness. Neither is a confidentiality or authorization issue. The change adds no logging of content and no new disk or network surface. It does not touch prefix-cache storage (T-041), the encryption path (T-008), or attestation/authorization.

Unverified contract: `StopHoldback`, `CBv2StopStringScope`, and `ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope` live in the libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule. Its pointer moved from aee6ebb to 2beb401, and the diff is not supplied. The libs/mlx and libs/mlx-swift pointers also moved, and their diffs are not supplied either. Submodule contents (Metal kernels, MLX, the SDK) are unreviewed, so I cannot confirm they do not affect KV cache encryption, memory accounting, or media decode limits. Whether `stopStringScope` is a property that exists on EngineV2Bridge, and whether the scoped replay matches the engine's scan, is not visible here. A minor consistency risk remains: the replay uses `scan.text` length to locate the tail, so a mismatch could return nil or a wrong candidate. That affects only a diagnostic and reporting field.

inference.md changes are documentation only (the MiMo/Flint text is shown as context; the only listed range is the stop row at 1846, which falls outside the supplied units). I identified no concrete regression. Deeper review is warranted for the three bumped submodules.
